chapters.title: The Righteousness of God Revealed
chapters.html:
Romans 1

Greeting

1Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus, called to be an apostle, set apart for the gospel of God,

2which He promised beforehand through His prophets in the holy Scriptures,

3concerning His Son, who was descended from the seed of David according to the flesh,

4who was appointed Son of God in power according to the Spirit of holiness by the resurrection of the dead: Jesus Christ our Lord.

5Through Him we have received grace and apostleship to bring about the obedience of faith among all the Gentiles, for the sake of His name,

6and you also are among them, called to belong to Jesus Christ.

7To all who are in Rome, loved by God, called to be saints: grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

Paul's Wish to Come to Rome

8First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because your faith is being proclaimed in all the world.

9For God, whom I serve in my spirit in the gospel of His Son, is my witness how unceasingly I mention you,

10always in my prayers, asking that somehow, now at last, by the will of God, I may succeed in coming to you.

11For I long to see you, so that I may share with you some spiritual gift to strengthen you —

12that is, so that we may be encouraged together among you, each by the other's faith, both yours and mine.

13I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, that I have often planned to come to you, and have been prevented until now, so that I might have some fruit among you too, as I have among the rest of the Gentiles.

14I am a debtor both to Greeks and to non-Greeks, both to the wise and to the foolish.

15So, for my part, I am eager to preach the gospel to you also who are in Rome.

The Power of God for Salvation

16For I am not ashamed of the gospel, because it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes, to the Jew first and also to the Greek.

17For in it the righteousness of God is revealed from faith to faith, as it is written: "The righteous will live by faith."

The Wrath of God Revealed

18For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all the ungodliness and unrighteousness of people who suppress the truth by their unrighteousness.

19For what can be known about God is plain to them, because God has shown it to them.

20Ever since the creation of the world His invisible qualities, His eternal power and divine nature, have been clearly seen, understood through what He has made. So they are without excuse;

21for although they knew God, they did not glorify Him as God or give Him thanks. Instead, their thinking became empty, and their senseless heart was darkened.

22Claiming to be wise, they became fools,

23and exchanged the glory of the immortal God for an image made in the likeness of mortal man and of birds and four-footed animals and creeping things.

24So God handed them over, in the desires of their hearts, to impurity, to the dishonoring of their bodies among themselves.

25They exchanged the truth of God for the lie, and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is blessed forever. Amen.

26For this reason God handed them over to dishonorable passions. Their women exchanged natural relations for what is contrary to nature,

27and the men likewise gave up natural relations with women and were inflamed with desire for one another, men with men committing what is shameful, and receiving in themselves the due penalty for their error.

28Since they did not think God worth acknowledging, God handed them over to a worthless mind, to do what ought not to be done.

29They are filled with every kind of unrighteousness, wickedness, greed and malice; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit and spite. They are gossips,

30slanderers, haters of God, insolent, arrogant, boastful, inventors of evil, disobedient to parents,

31senseless, faithless, heartless, ruthless.

32Though they know God's righteous decree, that those who do such things deserve death, they not only do them but also approve of those who practice them.

Notes

  • vv3–4 "descended from the seed of David according to the flesh… appointed Son of God in power… by the resurrection of the dead" — two lines set side by side: according to the flesh, according to the Spirit of holiness. Horisthentos, appointed, is the verb of Peter and Paul in Acts, the one appointed by God to be judge (Acts 10:42), a man whom He has appointed… by raising Him from the dead (17:31). Many English Bibles have declared. Either way He is already His Son in v3; what the resurrection marks is Son of God in power. Ex anastaseōs nekrōn, word for word from a resurrection of dead ones: Paul names Christ's rising as the resurrection of the dead, not only His own.

  • v17 "the righteousness of God is revealed from faith to faith" — dikaiosynē theou can be God's own righteousness, His faithfulness to what He promised beforehand (v2), or the righteousness that comes from God to the one who believes. The letter goes on to use it both ways (3:5, 3:21–22). Pistis is both faith and faithfulness: the faithfulness of God in 3:3 is the same word. Ek pisteōs eis pistin, from faith to faith, has no verb, and the range is wide: from God's faithfulness to our faith, from one believer to the next, or faith from first to last.

  • v17 "The righteous will live by faith" — Habakkuk 2:4. The Hebrew has the righteous will live by his faithfulness, the righteous man's own; the Greek has ek pisteōs mou, by My faithfulness, God's. Paul quotes neither pronoun, and his three words can be read the righteous will live by faith or the one who is righteous by faith will live. In Galatians 3:11–12 he sets it beside the person who does them shall live by them (Leviticus 18:5), where by goes with live.

  • vv21–23 "their thinking became empty… exchanged the glory of the immortal God for an image made in the likeness of" — the words of Israel's own idolatry. Emataiōthēsan, became empty, is the Greek of Jeremiah 2:5, went after emptiness and became empty. Ēllaxan tēn doxan… en homoiōmati is Psalm 106:20 in the Greek, the golden calf: They exchanged their Glory for the image of an ox that eats grass (also Jeremiah 2:11). Image and likeness are the words of humankind's making (Genesis 1:26), and the list runs back through its creatures: man, birds, animals, creeping things. Paul tells the nations' fall in Israel's words, and in chapter 2 turns to the one who judges them.

  • vv24, 26, 28 "God handed them over" — paredōken autous, three times. The wrath of God… revealed (v18) is shown here as God giving people over to what they chose. It is the verb of the gospel: Christ was handed over for our trespasses (4:25), and God did not spare His own Son but handed Him over for us all (8:32), paredōken auton, the same form.

chapters.title: God's Righteous Judgment
chapters.html:
Romans 2

You Who Judge

1So you are without excuse, whoever you are, you who judge. For in judging another you condemn yourself, because you who judge do the very same things.

2We know that the judgment of God rightly falls on those who do such things.

3Do you suppose, you who judge those who do such things and yet do them yourself, that you will escape the judgment of God?

4Or do you despise the riches of His kindness and forbearance and patience, not knowing that God's kindness is leading you to repentance?

5But by your hardness and your unrepentant heart you are storing up wrath for yourself on the day of wrath, when the righteous judgment of God will be revealed.

6He will repay each one according to his deeds:

7to those who by patience in doing good seek glory and honor and immortality, eternal life;

8but to those who are self-seeking and disobey the truth and obey unrighteousness, wrath and fury.

9There will be trouble and distress for every human being who does evil, the Jew first and also the Greek,

10but glory and honor and peace for everyone who does good, the Jew first and also the Greek.

11For God shows no partiality.

The Law and the Heart

12All who have sinned without the Law will also perish without the Law, and all who have sinned under the Law will be judged by the Law.

13For it is not the hearers of the Law who are righteous before God; it is the doers of the Law who will be justified.

14When Gentiles, who do not have the Law by birth, do what the Law requires, they are a law to themselves, even though they do not have the Law.

15They show that the work of the Law is written on their hearts, while their conscience bears witness with them, and their thoughts accuse or even defend them among themselves,

16on the day when, according to my gospel, God judges the secrets of people through Christ Jesus.

You Who Call Yourself a Jew

17But if you call yourself a Jew, and rely on the Law and boast in God,

18and know His will and approve what is excellent, because you are instructed from the Law,

19and are sure that you yourself are a guide to the blind, a light to those in darkness,

20an instructor of the foolish, a teacher of children, because you have in the Law the embodiment of knowledge and truth —

21you, then, who teach someone else, do you not teach yourself? You who preach that one must not steal, do you steal?

22You who say that one must not commit adultery, do you commit adultery? You who detest idols, do you rob temples?

23You who boast in the Law, do you dishonor God by breaking the Law?

24For, as it is written, "The name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you."

Circumcision of the Heart

25Circumcision is of value if you keep the Law; but if you break the Law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision.

26So if a man who is uncircumcised keeps the righteous requirements of the Law, will not his uncircumcision be reckoned as circumcision?

27The one who is uncircumcised by birth and fulfills the Law will judge you, who have the letter and circumcision and yet break the Law.

28For a Jew is not one outwardly, and circumcision is not what is outward, in the flesh.

29A Jew is one inwardly, and circumcision is of the heart, by the Spirit, not by the letter. His praise is not from people but from God.

Notes

  • v1 "So you are without excuse… you who judge" — anapologētos, the word that closed the case against the idolaters, So they are without excuse (1:20). The reader who has nodded through chapter 1 is now in the same place.

  • vv6, 13 "He will repay each one according to his deeds… the doers of the Law who will be justified" — v6 is the Greek of Psalm 62:12, You repay a man according to his work, and of Proverbs 24:12. Dikaiōthēsontai, will be justified, is the verb of dikaios, righteous, in the same verse: in Greek justify and righteous are one word family, and so is the righteousness of God (1:17). Paul says here that the doers of the Law will be justified, and in 3:20 that by works of the Law no flesh will be justified. The letter holds both sentences; chapters 3–4 are where it works out how.

  • vv14–15 "Gentiles, who do not have the Law by birth… the work of the Law is written on their hearts" — physei, by nature or by birth, stands between the two halves of the sentence and can go with either: Gentiles who by nature do what the Law requires, or Gentiles who do not have the Law by birth. Paul uses it of birth in Galatians 2:15, we who are Jews by birth, and this chapter's uncircumcised by birth (v27) is ek physeōs. Written on their hearts is the new covenant of Jeremiah 31:33, on their heart I will write it.

  • v24 "The name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you" — Isaiah 52:5 in the Greek, because of you… My name is blasphemed among the nations. The Hebrew has neither because of you nor among the nations: continually, all day long, My name is despised, while Israel is in exile. Paul reads the Greek's because of you against the one who teaches the Law and breaks it.

  • vv28–29 "circumcision is of the heart, by the Spirit… His praise is not from people but from God" — Moses had said Circumcise, then, the foreskin of your heart (Deuteronomy 10:16), and The LORD your God will circumcise your heart (30:6). Jew is from Judah, and Jacob's blessing plays on the name: Judah — you, your brothers shall praise (Genesis 49:8). Paul ends on the same thought: the true Jew's praise comes from God.

chapters.title: The Righteousness of God Through Faith
chapters.html:
Romans 3

God Is Faithful

1What advantage, then, has the Jew? Or what is the value of circumcision?

2Much in every way. First of all, they were entrusted with the words of God.

3What if some were unfaithful? Will their unfaithfulness nullify the faithfulness of God?

4By no means! Let God be true though every man is a liar, as it is written:
"so that You may be justified in Your words
and prevail when You are judged."

5But if our unrighteousness shows the righteousness of God, what shall we say? That God is unrighteous to inflict wrath? (I am speaking in human terms.)

6By no means! For then how could God judge the world?

7But if through my lie the truth of God abounds to His glory, why am I still being judged as a sinner?

8Why not say, then, "Let us do evil so that good may come"? Some slander us by claiming that we say so. Their condemnation is just.

No One Is Righteous

9What then? Are we any better off? Not at all. For we have already charged that all, both Jews and Greeks, are under sin,

10as it is written:
"There is no one righteous, not even one;

11there is no one who understands,
no one who seeks God.

12They have all turned aside; together they have become worthless;
there is no one who does good,
not even one.

13Their throat is an open grave;
with their tongues they deceive;
the venom of asps is under their lips.

14Their mouth is full of cursing and bitterness.

15Their feet are swift to shed blood;

16ruin and misery are in their paths,

17they have not known the way of peace.

18There is no fear of God before their eyes."

19Now we know that whatever the Law says, it says to those who are under the Law, so that every mouth may be stopped and the whole world may be held accountable to God.

20For by works of the Law no flesh will be justified in His sight, since through the Law comes the knowledge of sin.

The Righteousness of God Made Known

21But now, apart from the Law, the righteousness of God has been made known, witnessed by the Law and the Prophets:

22the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ for all who believe. For there is no distinction,

23since all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God,

24and are justified freely by His grace, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus,

25whom God set forth as an atonement cover, through faith, by His blood. This was to show His righteousness, because in His forbearance God had passed over the sins committed before,

26to show His righteousness at the present time, so that He might be righteous and the one who justifies the one who has faith in Jesus.

27Where, then, is boasting? It is shut out. By what kind of law? A law of works? No, but by the law of faith.

28For we reckon that a person is justified by faith apart from works of the Law.

29Or is God the God of Jews only? Is He not the God of Gentiles also? Yes, of Gentiles also,

30since God is one. He will justify the circumcised by faith and the uncircumcised through faith.

31Do we then nullify the Law through faith? By no means! On the contrary, we uphold the Law.

Notes

  • v4 "so that You may be justified in Your words and prevail when You are judged" — Psalm 51:4 in the Greek. The Hebrew has so that You are right when You speak, titsdaq, the verb of tsaddiq, righteous; the Greek puts it as dikaiōthēs, You may be justified. Here the one justified is God, and the word cannot mean made righteous: it is shown to be in the right, as in a court.

  • vv10–20 "There is no one righteous… by works of the Law no flesh will be justified in His sight" — the words of the Psalms. Vv10–12 are Psalm 14:1–3, where the Hebrew has there is no one who does good, not even one; Paul's first line puts righteous in the place of who does good. Swete's Greek of that psalm already carries every line of vv13–18 after its v3. V20 is Psalm 143:2, no one living will be justified before You in the Greek, no one living is righteous before You in the Hebrew, with by works of the Law added.

  • vv22, 26 "through faith in Jesus Christ… the one who has faith in Jesus" — dia pisteōs Iēsou Christou, word for word through the faith of Jesus Christ, and ton ek pisteōs Iēsou, the one of the faith of Jesus. The Greek can mean faith in Jesus Christ, or the faithfulness of Jesus Christ, His own: pistis is the word of the faithfulness of God in v3. In Galatians 2:16 Paul uses the same phrase twice and between them says we believed in Christ Jesus.

  • v25 "whom God set forth as an atonement cover… by His blood" — hilastērion, the word the Greek of Exodus and Leviticus gives the gold cover on the ark, You shall make a cover of pure gold (Exodus 25:17), where on the Day of Atonement the high priest sprinkles the blood (Leviticus 16:14–15); Hebrews 9:5 uses it so. It names the place of atonement; other English Bibles have propitiation or sacrifice of atonement. Proetheto, set forth, can also mean purposed, the verb of I have often planned (1:13): set forth in public, or planned beforehand.

  • v30 "since God is one" — heis ho theos, the Shema, Hear, Israel: the LORD our God, the LORD is one (Deuteronomy 6:4). Israel's confession that there is one God becomes Paul's reason that He is the God of the Gentiles too, and justifies both in the same way.

chapters.title: Abraham Believed God
chapters.html:
Romans 4

Reckoned as Righteousness

1What then shall we say that Abraham, our forefather according to the flesh, has found?

2For if Abraham was justified by works, he has something to boast about — but not before God.

3For what does the Scripture say? "Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness."

4To one who works, his wages are not reckoned as a gift but as what is owed.

5But to one who does not work, but believes in Him who justifies the ungodly, his faith is reckoned as righteousness,

6just as David also speaks of the blessedness of the man to whom God reckons righteousness apart from works:

7"Blessed are those whose lawless deeds are forgiven,
and whose sins are covered;

8blessed is the man whose sin the Lord will never reckon."

Before He Was Circumcised

9Is this blessedness, then, for the circumcised only, or also for the uncircumcised? We say that faith was reckoned to Abraham as righteousness.

10How, then, was it reckoned? When he was circumcised, or when he was uncircumcised? Not when he was circumcised, but when he was uncircumcised.

11He received the sign of circumcision as a seal of the righteousness of the faith he had while he was uncircumcised, so that he would be the father of all who believe without being circumcised, so that righteousness would be reckoned to them also,

12and the father of the circumcised who are not only circumcised but who also walk in the footsteps of the faith that our father Abraham had while he was uncircumcised.

The Promise Through Faith

13For the promise to Abraham and to his seed, that he would be heir of the world, did not come through the Law but through the righteousness of faith.

14For if those who are of the Law are heirs, faith is made empty and the promise is nullified.

15For the Law brings about wrath; but where there is no law, there is no transgression either.

16That is why it is by faith, so that it may be by grace, and the promise may be sure for all his seed — not only for those who are of the Law, but also for those who are of the faith of Abraham, who is the father of us all,

17as it is written: "I have made you the father of many nations." He is our father in the sight of the God in whom he believed, who gives life to the dead and calls into being what does not exist.

18Hoping against hope, he believed that he would become the father of many nations, according to what had been said: "So shall your seed be."

19He did not weaken in faith when he considered his own body, as good as dead, since he was about a hundred years old, and the deadness of Sarah's womb.

20No unbelief made him waver concerning the promise of God, but he grew strong in faith, giving glory to God,

21fully convinced that God was able to do what He had promised.

22That is why "it was reckoned to him as righteousness."

Written for Us Also

23The words "it was reckoned to him" were not written for his sake alone,

24but for ours also. It will be reckoned to us who believe in Him who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead,

25who was handed over for our trespasses and raised for our justification.

Notes

  • vv3, 22–24 "Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness" — Genesis 15:6 in the Greek; the Hebrew reads He trusted in the LORD, and He reckoned it to him as righteousness. Logizomai, reckon, is an accounting word, a sum entered to someone's account, and it is the word of this chapter: eleven times, wages reckoned as owed (v4), faith reckoned as righteousness (v5), sin the Lord will never reckon (v8, Psalm 32:2). Paul's last turn is that the sentence about Abraham was not written for his sake alone.

  • v5 "Him who justifies the ungodly" — ton dikaiounta ton asebē, the very words the Greek Law forbids to a judge: you shall not justify the ungodly for gifts (Exodus 23:7, I will not acquit the guilty in the Hebrew), and woe to those who justify the ungodly for a bribe (Isaiah 5:23 in the Greek). Whoever justifies the wicked… is detestable to the LORD (Proverbs 17:15). What would be a crooked judge's sin, Paul says God does, and 3:26 has already said how He stays righteous in doing it.

  • vv13, 17 "heir of the world… I have made you the father of many nations" — Genesis promised Abraham the land (12:7; 15:18), and that in you all the families of the ground shall be blessed (Genesis 12:3); Paul names the inheritance the world. Pollōn ethnōn, many nations, is Genesis 17:5 in the Greek (the Hebrew has a roar of nations), and ethnē is the word this letter has been translating Gentiles (1:5, 13; 2:14; 3:29). The promise that Abraham would be the father of many nations is, in Paul's Greek, a promise that he would be father of the Gentiles.

  • v17 "who gives life to the dead and calls into being what does not exist" — kalountos ta mē onta hōs onta, word for word calling the things that are not as being. It can be the call of creation, things brought into being by a word, or God speaking of what does not yet exist as though it did, as He named Abraham father of many nations before he had a son. The two halves of the line are what Abraham faced: his body as good as dead (v19), and a son who did not yet exist.

  • vv20–21 "giving glory to God, fully convinced that God was able" — the reverse of the nations in chapter 1, who knew God and did not glorify Him as God (1:21), and who served the creature rather than the Creator (1:25). Abraham gave glory to God and believed Him as the One who gives life to the dead (v17).

speech.text: Romans 4
Reckoned as Righteousness
What then shall we say that Abraham, our forefather according to the flesh, has found?
For if Abraham was justified by works, he has something to boast about — but not before God.
For what does the Scripture say? "Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness."
To one who works, his wages are not reckoned as a gift but as what is owed.
But to one who does not work, but believes in Him who justifies the ungodly, his faith is reckoned as righteousness,
just as David also speaks of the blessedness of the man to whom God reckons righteousness apart from works:
"Blessed are those whose lawless deeds are forgiven, and whose sins are covered;
blessed is the man whose sin the Lord will never reckon."
Before He Was Circumcised
Is this blessedness, then, for the circumcised only, or also for the uncircumcised? We say that faith was reckoned to Abraham as righteousness.
How, then, was it reckoned? When he was circumcised, or when he was uncircumcised? Not when he was circumcised, but when he was uncircumcised.

He received the sign of circumcision as a seal of the righteousness of the faith he had while he was uncircumcised, so that he would be the father of all who believe without being circumcised, so that righteousness would be reckoned to them also,
and the father of the circumcised who are not only circumcised but who also walk in the footsteps of the faith that our father Abraham had while he was uncircumcised.
The Promise Through Faith
For the promise to Abraham and to his seed, that he would be heir of the world, did not come through the Law but through the righteousness of faith.
For if those who are of the Law are heirs, faith is made empty and the promise is nullified.
For the Law brings about wrath; but where there is no law, there is no transgression either.

That is why it is by faith, so that it may be by grace, and the promise may be sure for all his seed — not only for those who are of the Law, but also for those who are of the faith of Abraham, who is the father of us all,
as it is written: "I have made you the father of many nations." He is our father in the sight of the God in whom he believed, who gives life to the dead and calls into being what does not exist.
Hoping against hope, he believed that he would become the father of many nations, according to what had been said: "So shall your seed be."
He did not weaken in faith when he considered his own body, as good as dead, since he was about a hundred years old, and the deadness of Sarah's womb.
No unbelief made him waver concerning the promise of God, but he grew strong in faith, giving glory to God,
fully convinced that God was able to do what He had promised.
That is why "it was reckoned to him as righteousness."
Written for Us Also
The words "it was reckoned to him" were not written for his sake alone,
but for ours also. It will be reckoned to us who believe in Him who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead,
who was handed over for our trespasses and raised for our justification.
